title: Hummingbird Payments renewal + edge acceleration check-in
summary: Quarterly renewal/check-in focused on a 6-month capacity uplift, adding EU and APAC edge nodes, and discussing onprem/V P C constraints. Team agreed to pilot an EU private node, run latency benchmarks, and receive a revised quote for a short-term contract extension.
topics: next steps: quote, security docs, benchmark run
action_items: Alex Romero (Redwood AE): Send revised 6-month uplift quote including burst capacity and EU/APAC add-on by 2026-11-21
Priya Shah (Redwood SE): Schedule benchmark run and provide test harness + sample prompts; target window 2026-11-24 to 2026-11-26
Maya Chen (Hummingbird CTO): Share network architecture diagram and firewall egress constraints by 2026-11-20
Liam O'Connor (CSM): Produce failover playbook doc and proposed canary rollout timeline by 2026-11-30
next_steps: Redwood to deliver revised quote and capacity plan
Customer to approve pilot scope for EU private node
Run latency/cost benchmark during agreed window
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-17
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 43 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Alex Romero (Redwood AE); Priya Shah (Redwood SE); Liam O'Connor (CSM) -- Maya Chen (Hummingbird CTO); Jon Rivera (Head of Infra); Samir Patel (Procurement)

Summary (auto): quick check-in ahead of renewal to align on capacity, regions, and security gating. Not a formal contract signature call but alignment toward a 6-month bridge and pilot.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Alex here, Priya, Liam on the Redwood side.
[00:07] Maya: Hi — Maya here, Jon, Samir. Good to see you.
[00:12] Alex (Redwood): Awesome. We're here to go over the renewal cadence, the capacity uplift ask you sent last week, and the region add — EU plus APAC edge activation, is that right?
[00:24] Jon (Hummingbird): Yep. We're seeing token growth from our fraud detection model, and the PR spikes are hitting EU customers first so we need regional reduction in roundtrip.
[00:34] Priya (Redwood): Understood. On the uplift numbers you gave (roughly 2.5x baseline token throughput) — we sketched a couple options: a dedicated uplift pool vs burst capacity on hosted. Dedicated gives more predictable tail latencies, hosted + burst is cheaper but can have variability.
[00:48] Maya: Latency is our top success metric for the checkout flow. If latency slips more than 80ms at p95 we get a measurable drop in conversion. Cost is secondary but still material.
[01:02] Jon: Also note we need data egress limitations — our infra team won't allow open egress to public endpoints from EU region, so we might need a private V P C setup or onprem box.
[01:15] Priya (Redwood): Right — we can do Redwood Private in an EU region, or a V P C peering approach for hosted, or an onprem package. Each has different lead times: hosted bursts in hours, Dedicated in days, Private or onprem can take weeks for network/setup and K M S integration.
[01:33] Samir (Procurement): On contracting — we'd prefer a 6-month bridge rather than a full 12-month commit. Can you support a shorter term with a defined uplift?
[01:41] Alex (Redwood): Yes, we proposed a 6-month uplift option in the last deck — we can draft a short-term amendment with pro-rated committed capacity and burst pool. We'll include options for EU add-on and APAC early-access pricing.
[01:54] Maya: What's the expected provisioning time for an EU private node if we go that route?
[01:58] Priya (Redwood): For a private EU node with customer network (V P C), typical is 3-4 weeks assuming network peering and firewall rules are in place; if you need H S M/K M S integration for keys it's closer to 5-6 weeks. There can be some back-and-forth with networking.
[02:14] Jon: We can probably unblock basic peering within a week, but the H S M integration will take longer. For the pilot we only need the node to accept traffic from EU to measure p95 latencies, not full H S M.
[02:27] Priya (Redwood): That works. We can provision a private node with temporary keyholders and then migrate keys later. We'll flag the security team.
[02:35] Alex (Redwood): On performance — we also recommend a short benchmark run with your worst-case prompt set. Priya, can you talk about the test harness?
[02:41] Priya (Redwood): Sure. We'll provide a small harness that mimics your checkout flow: short prompt generations, KV cache warm-up, and sustained throughput at X TPS. We'll run tests from both US and EU endpoints. The goal is to measure p50/p95 latencies and token cost under continuous load.
[02:58] Maya: Perfect. Do you handle simulated cold cache and warmed cache runs? We see big differences.
[03:04] Priya: Yep — we'll do cold start, warmed K V cash (sorry, K V cache) and steady state. The script will be in a Git repo we share, and you can run it from your infra or we can run it from Redwood side against the pilot node.
[03:18] Jon: One pain we had previously with another vendor (CloudEndpointX) was inconsistent tokenization causing cost variance. How deterministic is Redwood across model versions?
[03:28] Priya: We provide pinned model versions for serving; the runtime keeps stable tokenizer kernels. If you need, we can lock to a specific model sha. We'll also surface per-token breakdown in Console so you can reconcile spend.
[03:40] Samir (Procurement): On security docs — we need SOC 2 attestation, audit logs, S S O and S A M L support, and K M S integration notes. Do you have a security pack we can review?
[03:51] Liam (CSM): Yes — I'll share the security brief, SOC 2 report summary, and an H S M/K M S integration checklist after this call. Expect it by tomorrow.
[03:59] Maya: Great. Also, can you show network egress IPs so our firewall team can pre-allow?
[04:05] Priya (Redwood): We can provide a CIDR list for hosted endpoints and V P C peering guidance. For Private nodes, there are dedicated endpoints inside your network so fewer egress rules.
[04:16] Jon: About cost — if we do dedicated uplift vs hosted burst what are rough unit numbers? We've been on hosted so far.
[04:23] Alex (Redwood): Roughly speaking, dedicated committed capacity lowers per-token cost by 20-35% depending on utilization. Hosted burst has a higher per-token rate but no commit. We'll include a cost projection table in the quote showing token/unit economics at 50/75/90% utilization for both options.
[04:40] Maya: I'm also worried about fallbacks — if EU capacity gets saturated do you do automated routing to US? What's the impact on latency for EU users?
[04:47] Priya (Redwood): We support policy-based routing: fallback to a compatible model in another region, or fall back to a smaller model with lower latency. Both are configurable; we'll surface estimated latency impact in the benchmark results.
[04:59] Jon: For the pilot, can we test a canary route that sends 5% traffic to the new EU node and keep the rest on existing?
[05:05] Priya (Redwood): Absolutely — we can set a canary split and monitor p95 and error rates in Console.
[05:10] Samir: On procurement side — payment terms: can you do net 45 with a PO? And how about contract amendment for the 6-month bridge?
[05:17] Alex (Redwood): Net 45 is okay; we'll work with legal on a 6-month amendment that references the existing MSA. I'll include payment term options in the quote.
[05:26] Maya: One more technical: we use an internal reranker post-generation. Does Redwood support streaming output so we can start reranker earlier?
[05:33] Priya (Redwood): Yes, streaming is supported. We have streaming APIs and function-calling style hooks to pipe outputs earlier; we'll include recommended patterns in the test harness.
[05:44] Jon: Any blockers on your end to start pilot quickly?
[05:47] Alex (Redwood): We need your network diagram and a signed amendment or LOI for the 6-month uplift to carve inventory. Once we have that we can schedule provisioning and bench runs.
[05:57] Maya: We'll get the diagram and a signed LOI. Samir, can procurement move on a short LOI?
[06:02] Samir: Yes we can do a LOI for a 6-month uplift; legal will need to see the amendment. I'll try to get that by 11/20.
[06:10] Priya (Redwood): Great. We'll tentatively schedule benchmarking for 11/24-11/26; we'll share the harness repo and test plan by Friday.
[06:19] Alex (Redwood): Ok let's capture action items. Liam will share security docs; Priya will prepare harness; Alex will issue quote. Any remaining competitor concerns?
[06:28] Maya: We are also talking to FastServeAI on region pricing; they pitched a cheaper EU node but had higher error rates. We want reliable p95.
[06:37] Alex (Redwood): Noted. We'll make sure the quote includes SLA references and expected p95 targets.
[06:43] Jon: Small thing — can we get a short runbook for failover? We need simple steps for ops.
[06:48] Liam (CSM): I'll draft a one-page failover playbook and include a canary rollback checklist.
[06:54] Maya: Great, thanks.
[06:56] Samir: On billing — if we go 6 months, do you provide monthly statements with unit breakdown?
[07:02] Alex (Redwood): Yes monthly invoices with token-line items and per-route breakdown. We'll also include a projection in the quote.
[07:09] Maya: Ok, can we confirm next sync date?
[07:12] Alex (Redwood): How about Monday 11/29 at 10am PT?
[07:16] Maya: Works for me.
[07:18] Jon: Works.
[07:20] Samir: Yep.
[07:22] Alex (Redwood): Cool. Quick recap: Redwood to send revised 6-month amendment quote, include EU & APAC add-on pricing, cost projection table, SLA language; Redwood SE to provide test harness and schedule bench; customer to provide network diagram and LOI; security docs from CSM. Follow-up 11/29.
[07:37] Maya: Thanks everyone.
[07:39] Alex (Redwood): Thanks, talk soon.

Notes on transcript: occasional garbling where acronyms were transcribed as spaced letters (V P C, K M S) and 'K V cash' for KV cache; speaker turns sometimes labeled by role.
